messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED (pagerduty): Network / LB health degradation - TLS handshake failures observed across multiple frontends. Severity: P1. PagerDuty link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-2248

Maya (oncall): Acked. I'm on it — grabbing logs and routing table. ETA 5m. @pagerduty please stop escalation for now, I'm taking lead.

Arun: seeing alerts for LB target unhealthy in cloud console. HTTP(S) LB shows backend group 'inference-pool-1' with 23/30 healthy -> 7 unhealthy on port 443. Any recent cert rotations or config pushes?

Jess: Confirmed from LB health checks: TLS handshake errors, handshake failure code 525 in logs. Health check probe logs: 
```
2026-03-14T14:02:11Z health-checker request to 10.0.12.34:443 - TLS alert handshake_failure
2026-03-14T14:02:12Z health-checker request to 10.0.12.35:443 - OK
```
Looks like a subset of backends failing TLS during handshake. No HTTP 5xx returned — upstream drops.

Tom: I pushed a cert rotation to staging earlier but not to prod. Did we have any automated cert deploy job run? @Liu did we have any automated renewals?

Liu: We rotated certs for private deploys last night; production LB cert was scheduled but the AWS ACM job errored during validation (DNS validation failed). I see an error in the cert-provisioner logs: 
```
2026-03-14T01:10:02Z cert-provisioner: validation failed for cert apis.redwood.ai - DNS record not found
```
If ACM didn't attach the new cert, some backends may still be presenting old certs or closing connections.

Maya (oncall): Ok, that explains TLS handshake failures. How many customers affected? Is this internal-only or going to public API endpoints?

Jess: Metrics show elevated client TLS errors spikes starting 14:01 UTC, affecting our public API frontends in us-west1 and eu-west1. Rough ballpark: 6-12% error rate for token-generation routes; some large customers reporting increased latencies and failed requests.

Support-ops: Notified two enterprise customers about degraded API availability via status page and direct messages. We have an incident banner live: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2248

Arun: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Roll back any recent LB config changes (none recorded for prod in last 24h) 2) Force attach a known-good certificate to LB 3) Fallback route: shift traffic to secondary LB that still has valid certs (lb-secondary.redwood.ai) 4) Lower DNS TTL if we need to repoint CNAMEs. I'll take 2+3.

Maya (oncall): I'll coordinate with Support and Alerts. Tom, can you validate certificate contents from one failing backend? Run openssl check: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.34:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -brief
```
Paste output if you can.

Tom: Running now...
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.34:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -brief
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
verify error:num=10:certificate has expired
notAfter=Mar 13 23:59:59 2026 GMT
---
SSL handshake has read 2103 bytes and written 326 bytes
```
This backend cert expired yesterday (Mar 13). That matches the failure window.

Liu: ACM shows the new cert pending DNS validation and never attached. The automated job created a CNAME under _acme-challenge... but our DNS provider's API returned 409 due to recent rate limits and the record was never created. There's a race in the cert-provisioner.

Arun: Immediate action: attach an existing valid cert, fail traffic to lb-secondary. I'm going to attach cert-2025-12 (valid until 2027) to the frontend and kick a rolling restart of the unhealthy instances.

Maya (oncall): Go for it. I'll page escalation if attach fails. Support-ops keep customers posted.

(1 minute later) incident-bot: PagerDuty note: Maya acknowledged. Escalation paused.

Arun: Attached cert-2025-12 to LB frontend. Re-checking health...

Jess: Health probe status improving: now 27/30 healthy. TLS handshake errors dropping. Graph: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingress/tls-handshakes?from=now-1h

Support-ops: Customers updated: "We're seeing improvements; engineers applied a temporary cert to frontends while we fix the provisioning race. We'll follow up when DNS validation job is re-run."

Maya (oncall): Good. Switching to follow-up actions: 
- Run cert-provisioner with manual DNS record creation to finish validation.
- File an ops bug to add retry/backoff to DNS provider API calls.
- Postmortem owner: Arun.
- Notify SRE oncall lead for continuous monitoring.

Tom: Manual DNS record added and validation completed. ACM successfully issued new cert; scheduling attach during low traffic in 10m. Recommendation: add a health-check-based automatic failover to secondary LB if cert attach fails in the future.

Liu: I'll add retries + exponential backoff to the cert-provisioner today and open a PR. Also increasing logging around validation failures.

Maya (oncall): On-call handoff in 30m — Arun will be primary for mitigation steps and postmortem. I'll leave paged alerts unrouted to avoid noisy escalations.

Arun: Attaching new cert now to prod frontends; syncing with infra agent.

(5m later) Jess: New cert attached and propagated. Health stable 30/30. TLS error rate back to baseline.

Support-ops: Status update posted: incident mitigated, certificate rotation issue identified as root cause, postmortem pending. Ticket created: OPS-613.

Maya (oncall): Final notes before handoff: Impact: 6-12% increased request failures for generation endpoints across US/EU for ~25 minutes. Root cause: cert-provisioner DNS validation race + DNS provider rate limiting prevented automated cert attach; expired cert on subset of backends. Mitigation: attach known-good cert + failover to secondary LB; manual DNS validation completed.

Arun: I'll own the postmortem, action items, and ETA for a durable fix. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (pagerduty): INC-2248 - marked resolved by Maya (oncall).

Maya (oncall): Closing the thread. I'll hand off to Arun for the postmortem and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
